title: Souvenance — a personal memory engine that checks each memory against its source, and the SOURCED integrity benchmark
description:
A self-hosted personal memory engine for AI assistants. Events are stored in an append-only PostgreSQL log owned by the subject; memories, embeddings and a bi-temporal knowledge graph are recomputable projections of that log. A language model proposes each memory with a verbatim excerpt; code checks the excerpt against the source before writing, and applies the same proof gate to identity links. Nightly consolidation runs on a swappable AI backend, and the memory is served through MCP.

This archive includes the research/ folder: position papers, pre-registered evaluation protocols, and SOURCED (draft v0.1), a benchmark of write-time integrity for personal memory on synthetic lives, with first results for three memory systems (Souvenance, Mem0, Graphiti). Limits stated with the results: every life comes from one generator written by the author; the model judge did not pass its pre-registered validation (kappa 0.54 for a threshold of 0.70); one model family writes, reads and judges; no ablation of the identity-link gate; LoCoMo not run end to end. Development is paused at this release.
